newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: IMF suspends standby loan to Pakistan - minister.
newsitem.headline: IMF suspends standby loan to Pakistan - minister.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund has suspended its standby loan to Pakistan, Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz said on Friday.
"The standby arrangement has been suspended," Aziz told a news conference after an IMF mission ended two weeks of discussions with the Pakistani government.
Aziz said Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif's government, which took office last month after winning February 3 elections, would announce an industrial revival package in the next few days.
"We will supplement the demand side measures with supply side measures," he said. "This we hope will give a major boost to our economy."

The IMF mission, reviewing Pakistan's economic performance before deciding whether to recommend the release this month of the next $122 million standby tranche, left Islamabad earlier on Friday without making any public statement.

The fund resumed the standby loan in December after a caretaker government promised to cut the budget deficit to four percent of gross domestic product in 1996/97 (July-June) from 6.3 percent in 1995/96.
Aziz and Sharif have both indicated that they believe the four percent target cannot be met within the deadline.
"The mission welcomed the government's intention to move forward on a bold programme of structural reform," a government statement released at Aziz's news conference said.

"It endorses the government's desire to move decisively to take radical measures for the reform of taxes and of tax administration as well as for accelerated privatisation and the revival of the industrial and agricultural sectors.

"The government's policy package, when implemented fully, will lay the basis for a transition to negotiations of a medium-term ESAF/EFF arrangement," it said, referring to IMF enhanced structural adjustment and extended fund facilities.
"It was decided that negotiations for the new arrangement could commence immediately after successful implementation of these policies," the statement concluded.
